steps.text: Combine black pepper, paprika, cayenne pepper, minced garlic, Dijon mustard, brown sugar, onion powder, and salt in a small bowl. Stir in 1 tablespoon olive oil to make a paste.
Spread paste over salmon fillets; set aside to marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Stir in onion; cook until tender and golden brown, about 10 minutes.
Heat a separate nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook salmon fillets in the hot skillet until golden brown on each side and no longer translucent in the center, about 4 minutes per side.
Pour caramelized onions and olive oil over salmon fillets to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Salmon with Caramelized Onions
raw_recipe.description: Salmon fillets are marinated with a spice paste and finished with caramelized onions in this quick and easy spicy salmon onion recipe.

review.reviewBody: Wow! This dish came out way better than I could have imagined. The paste forms a nice crust on the salmon making it have a cajun feel to it. The spiciness is nicely offset by the sweetness of the caramelized onions. It's also super simple to make. I did double the cayenne because I like spicy and omitted the onion powder (didn't have any.) I also used a whole onion which was the right choice. One note - if the salmon is thick then use a lower heat because the paste will burn the top while the inside remains raw.

Great Salmon recipe, I followed the recipe but seared the top first for 2 minutes then the skin, then baked in fan forced oven at 180 for approx 10 minutes, checking every 3. I read other comments & agree should thinly slice a whole onion, also to caralamise the onion I added a tablespoon of Red wine vinegar, it also adds sweetness. This worked really well & i will be making this again, thanks.

So good! Changed slightly by caramelizing 1/2 large chopped onion then added 3 cups fresh baby spinach; cooked on low till spinach was wilted; served spinach/onion on the side with Farro. Best of all though was the salmon itself! As above ... so good!!!

We're all but snowed in tonight, a little light on some ingredients, and too far from a grocery store, but we have a cupboard of some canned goods. I had to make TONS of changes and substitutions, but the resulting meal was still DELICIOUS!

Substitutions/Changes:
Canned salmon instead of salmon,
1/4th tsp lemon pepper instead of Dijon mustard,
molasses instead of brown sugar,
margarine instead of oil -- I had to add 2 Tbs more to keep things from burning,
two small onions sliced into rings instead of the minced onion and onion powder,
1/4 tsp garlic powder instead of minced garlic cloves,
reduced 1 1/2 tsp of black pepper to 1 tsp.

Still delicious even with all those changes! Next time, I'll make it with even less black pepper; it was almost too spicy for the version of this recipe I made. Excellent dinner for having almost nothing on hand.

Real good. The salmon topping is wonderful. I wanted to cut back on the calories from oil so I baked the salmon in a 400 degree oven for 25 minutes. I thought the 1 1/2 tablespoons of minced onion was not enough for an ingredient that receives top billing in the title, so I diced about 1/3 c. onions. I will make this again.

Great Spicy Flavor!! I sauted the onions and garlic then tossed the remaining ingredients in the pan with a little extra EVOO to loosen to spreading consistency. Then put the salmon on a baking dish, spread the onion mixture over the fish then baked @ 400 to our desired doneness.

We will definitely be making this salmon again! I baked it (@ 400 for 15min) instead of skillet frying it, and it still turned out amazing! As one reviewer suggested, I doubled the cayenne - it was HOT, just how my husband likes it!

I loved this. Super easy. I like spicy so after reading reviews I doubled the cayenne pepper to one teaspoon but it was really really hot. I will not double that next time! 
The only other thing I changed was to sauté the onion in butter rather than olive oil. It gave it a added kick of sweet. I used 1 tbl spoon of butter and half a sweet onion. Delish.
I put my broiler on low and cooked the salmon skin side down. It took about 8 mins and the skin stuck to the tin foil that covered the pan and it was easy to slide fish off the skin and serve... and also no clean up. I just threw the tin foil away. 
I will def make this again!!

This recipe is very good and quite spicy for people who aren't used to eating spicy foods. The second time I made this recipe, I omitted the onions and cooked the salmon in the oven at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes, and also added some maple syrup in the bottom of the pan. I do find the rub a bit too thick (perhaps it makes too much for 2 salmon fillets?). I just removed most of the rub when I ate it and it was still quite tasty.

This is our absolute favorite recipe. I only put a smidge of cayenne pepper in because the 1/4 tsp was way to much. I also coat the fish with the mixture a couple hours prior to cooking and put it back in the fridge. When I'm ready it goes in a 400 degree oven for 20-30 minutes!!! So Yummy Thanks for sharing this recipe!

Sugar in the "paste" made fish start to blacken so I added some water to pan. Served resulting "sauce" on fish. Used half a sliced onion per serving. Used regular paprika then added 1/2 t Hungarian paprika as well. Served with wilted spinach.
This is really good! I used dried minced onion. Thinly sliced a large vidalia onion as 1.5 Tbsp is not enough. Will definitely make this again.
The recipe was great. The only thing I added was mixed hot pepper flakes because we really like it spicy in my household..
delicious! If you like caramelized onions, recommend adding more. Will definitely be making again.

Pretty good! Definitely use butter to caramelize the onion, so much better. Upping the cayenne heat is a good thing for us too! Also, no fail for salmon, 400* for 15 min. So baked it for comfort zone, came out great! Will do again.
I didn't have Dijon mustard, but it is an easy recipe and was supper tasty
So easy to make and with the caramelized onions, it was super yummy!
